questions.q: Quick Sight dashboards read an Athena table over S3. They are slow and the Athena scan bill is high because many readers open them all day. What should the team do?

options.t: Create a larger Athena workgroup
options.why: Wrong: it does not stop repeated scans, so the cost stays.

options.t: Switch the dataset to direct query
options.why: Wrong: direct query runs Athena on every visual load, which is the cause of the problem.

options.t: Add more Quick Sight Author seats
options.why: Wrong: authors do not change how often the source is queried.

options.t: Import the dataset into SPICE on a schedule
options.why: Right: SPICE serves repeated queries from its in-memory copy, so Athena scans only at refresh.

questions.explain: SPICE removes repeated Athena scans and speeds up visuals.
questions.remember: Athena source with slow dashboards or a high scan bill → SPICE with a refresh schedule, not a bigger workgroup.
variants: Users must see the last few minutes of data → direct query.
Many concurrent readers on any source → SPICE.
Source must not be copied for compliance → direct query.

questions.q: A dashboard on a fast Redshift cluster must show data that is at most a few minutes old. The data may not be copied for compliance reasons. Which dataset mode fits?

options.t: Direct query
options.why: Right: it queries the source live (short cache), so nothing is copied and data is current.

options.t: SPICE with a daily full refresh
options.why: Wrong: it copies data and is only as fresh as the last refresh.

options.t: SPICE with a monthly schedule
options.why: Wrong: far too stale and still a copy.

options.t: File upload of a daily export
options.why: Wrong: uploaded files are always imported into SPICE and are stale.

questions.explain: Near real time or no-copy requirements point to direct query.
questions.remember: Near-real-time or cannot-copy data on a fast source → direct query. Otherwise SPICE.
variants: Fastest SPICE option is a 15-minute incremental refresh (Enterprise).
Direct query visuals stop waiting after 2 minutes.
Source is slow or huge → SPICE if it fits.

questions.q: A Glue job loads a fact table at unpredictable times each night. Dashboards must update right after the load finishes. What is the best design?

options.t: An hourly SPICE schedule
options.why: Wrong: it may run before or long after the load finishes.

options.t: Daily schedule at the latest possible time
options.why: Wrong: it can miss a late load and delays every other night.

options.t: EventBridge on job completion triggers a Lambda that calls `CreateIngestion`
options.why: Right: the API refresh runs as soon as the data lands.

options.t: Switch to direct query on the raw files
options.why: Wrong: the S3 connector cannot query directly, S3 data is always imported into SPICE.

questions.explain: Event-driven refresh through the CreateIngestion API.
questions.remember: ETL finishes at random times → EventBridge/Step Functions → Lambda → `CreateIngestion`.
variants: Fixed ETL time → a normal daily SPICE schedule.
Check refresh status → `DescribeIngestion`.
Stop a running refresh → `CancelIngestion`.

questions.q: A company's PostgreSQL database sits in a private subnet with no public endpoint. Quick Sight must build datasets from it. What is required?

options.t: Allow the Quick Sight public IP range in the DB security group
options.why: Wrong: that works only for databases with a public endpoint.

options.t: A VPC connection, which creates ENIs in your subnets, plus security group rules
options.why: Right: Quick reaches private IPs through its network interfaces in the VPC.

options.t: Upload a CSV export every day
options.why: Wrong: it works but is manual and not a connection to the database.

options.t: An Athena data source on the database
options.why: Wrong: Athena does not read a private PostgreSQL database directly.

questions.explain: Private sources need a VPC connection.
questions.remember: Private database → VPC connection (ENIs, security groups, Enterprise). Public endpoint → allow the Quick IP range for that Region.
variants: Public endpoint, timeouts → check you used the IP range of the right Region.
Private hostname will not resolve → add Route 53 Resolver endpoints or use the IP.
On-premises DB → VPC connection plus Direct Connect or VPN.

questions.q: A SPICE dataset on an Enterprise account uses incremental refresh with a 3-day look-back window. Users report that edits to rows from last month never appear. What is the cause and fix?

options.t: SPICE capacity is full; buy more capacity
options.why: Wrong: a full pool makes ingestion fail, it does not skip old rows.

options.t: The schedule is exclusive; add a daily schedule
options.why: Wrong: exclusive schedules affect which schedules you can add, not which rows change.

options.t: Incremental refresh is not supported on SQL sources
options.why: Wrong: it is supported on SQL sources such as Redshift and Athena.

options.t: Changes older than the window are not picked up; widen the window or run a periodic full refresh
options.why: Right: only rows inside the look-back window are deleted and re-inserted.

questions.explain: Incremental refresh replaces only rows inside the look-back window.
questions.remember: Old-row updates missing after incremental refresh → widen the look-back window or run a full refresh.
variants: Late-arriving updates from yesterday → a look-back window that covers them.
Deleting the incremental config triggers a full refresh.
S3 or file datasets → full refresh only.

questions.q: Regional managers must see only the rows for their own region in one shared dataset. One VP must see every region. How is this done in Quick Sight?

options.t: Column-level security on the region column
options.why: Wrong: CLS hides columns, not rows.

options.t: Create a separate dashboard per region
options.why: Wrong: it multiplies maintenance and does not enforce row access on the dataset.

options.t: A row-level security rules dataset mapping user or group to region, with a NULL region row for the VP
options.why: Right: users see matching rows only, and a NULL value means all values.

options.t: Dataset-level filter on the region field
options.why: Wrong: a dataset filter applies to everyone equally.

questions.explain: RLS rules dataset with a NULL rule row for full access.
questions.remember: Different rows per user or group → RLS rules dataset (Enterprise); NULL in a rule field = all values. Hiding fields → CLS.
variants: Hide a salary column from analysts → column-level security.
RLS works only on text fields; cast numbers or dates to string.
Dataset owners always see all data.

questions.q: A SaaS company embeds a dashboard in its web app for 200 customers. Customers have no AWS or Quick identity and each must see only its own data. Which design fits?

options.t: Anonymous embedding with session tags and tag-based RLS
options.why: Right: tags passed at embed time filter rows per session, with no user accounts.

options.t: Registered-user embedding with one Quick user per customer user
options.why: Wrong: needs accounts for every customer user, which is heavy for this case.

options.t: Public (1-click) embedding
options.why: Wrong: it exposes all the data to everyone, with no per-viewer RLS.

options.t: One AWS account per customer
options.why: Wrong: strongest isolation but far too much overhead for 200 tenants.

questions.explain: Anonymous embedding plus tag-based RLS scales to many tenants.
questions.remember: No identities and per-tenant data → anonymous embedding + session tags + tag-based RLS. Internal staff with SSO → registered-user embedding.
variants: Tenants need their own logins and separated assets → namespaces.
Public non-sensitive stats → public embedding.
Embed URL fails on refresh → URLs are single-use, generate a new one.

questions.q: A company serves 2,000 external customers who each open a dashboard about once a month. They are not registered Quick users. Which pricing choice is cheapest and supported?

options.t: Per-user Reader roles for all 2,000 customers
options.why: Wrong: about $6,000 a month versus about $1,000 with session pricing.

options.t: Reader session capacity (anonymous embedding)
options.why: Right: $250 for 500 sessions plus $0.50 per extra, about $1,000, and anonymous embedding needs session capacity.

options.t: Author Pro seats for every customer
options.why: Wrong: the most expensive role, and not meant for readers.

options.t: Buy extra SPICE capacity
options.why: Wrong: SPICE is storage and does not change how readers are billed.

questions.explain: Many occasional external readers → reader sessions.
questions.remember: Many occasional or external readers → session pricing. A reader above about 6 sessions a month is cheaper as a per-user Reader ($3). Anonymous embedding always needs sessions.
variants: 100 staff using it daily → per-user Reader.
`UnsupportedPricingPlanException` → buy session capacity.
Only two executives need AI summaries → Reader Pro for them.

questions.q: An Athena dataset in Quick Sight fails with an insufficient Lake Formation permissions error. The S3 buckets are already ticked in the Quick security settings. What is missing?

options.t: A larger SPICE capacity
options.why: Wrong: capacity errors are a different message.

options.t: A VPC connection
options.why: Wrong: Athena is reached through the service, not a VPC connection.

options.t: A new Athena workgroup
options.why: Wrong: a workgroup does not grant Lake Formation access.

options.t: A Lake Formation SELECT grant to the principal Quick uses
options.why: Right: S3 access alone is not enough for Lake Formation governed tables.

questions.explain: Lake Formation needs its own grant for the Quick principal.
questions.remember: Athena error on Lake Formation tables → grant LF SELECT to the Quick principal. S3 access denied → tick the data and results buckets. Encrypted bucket → allow `kms:Decrypt` for the Quick role.
variants: Access denied on S3 → check Security & permissions for data and results buckets.
Encrypted bucket fails → add the Quick role to the KMS key policy.
Cross-account S3 → bucket policy for the Quick role (and KMS policy).

questions.q: An analyst finds that anomaly detection is unavailable on one dataset but works on others. What is the most likely cause?

options.t: The dataset is in direct query mode
options.why: Wrong: this is not what blocks anomaly detection.

options.t: The dataset has too few columns
options.why: Wrong: column count is not the limit.

options.t: The dataset uses row-level security
options.why: Right: anomaly detection is not supported on datasets that use RLS.

options.t: The account is in the wrong Region
options.why: Wrong: Region does not disable it for one dataset.

questions.explain: Anomaly detection is not supported on RLS datasets.
questions.remember: Anomaly detection greyed out → check for RLS on the dataset.
variants: Email when a KPI crosses a number → threshold alert on a KPI or gauge visual.
Many dimensions in anomaly detection → many metrics, higher cost.
Alerts cannot fire faster than SPICE refreshes.
